run_kind: Reproduction: the author's checkers over the author's vectors
independent_execution_means: the run happened outside the maintainer's environment; it does NOT mean an independently authored checker or independently constructed vectors
prior_approval: none required, none sought, none claimed

manifest_preflight.note: byte-integrity preflight only; not the measured reproduction run

recorded_run.cwd: repository root of the pinned checkout
recorded_run.exit_code_meaning: every suite that ran matched its published expected verdicts; nothing wider

two_distinct_digest_constructions.note: these are different declared digest constructions over different file sets. They are recorded side by side under their own names and are deliberately NOT compared for equality.

case_count_note: suites[].cases is null and totals.cases_passed is 0 because the aggregate runner derives a declared case count from expected.json['cases'] or a cases/ directory. These two suites key expected.json by case name at top level and store inputs under records/ and sets/, so no count is derivable. Both checkers executed (returncode 0) and matched their published expected verdicts. '0 cases' means the case count is not declared in a shape this runner recognises, NOT that zero cases were graded. The graded file set is pinned by SHA-256 in report.corpus.suites.

supersedes.reason: that first attempt executed the same two suites with the same result, but its report recorded commit:null because the clone sat on a root-owned mount and the runner's plain `git rev-parse HEAD` subprocess was refused with 'detected dubious ownership'. commit_dirty:false there was produced by the same failure rather than by observing a clean tree. It is preserved unmodified and unpublished; this run was authorized by the owner as a new run identity and executed on a user-owned path.

establishes: the observed behavior of these pinned public checkers over these pinned public vectors in this environment
that the two suites ran outside the maintainer's environment and matched their published expected verdicts
does_not_establish: an independently authored implementation from the specification text
signature authentication beyond what the checkers actually test
AIREP interoperability or any Vaara x AIREP mapping result
endorsement by Vaara or its maintainer
